prompt: 37 yo F with history of epilepsy (on valproic acid and lamotrigine), recently diagnosed with tuberculosis, presents for treatment initiation; ID recommends starting isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide—begin standard RIPE therapy with her current antiepileptics?

rubric_items.text: Identifies rifampin enzyme induction as potentially substantially lowering both valproate and lamotrigine concentrations, increasing the risk of breakthrough seizures.

Recommends starting indicated TB therapy with an ID/neurology-coordinated interaction-management plan—monitoring antiseizure medication levels and seizure control and adjusting doses as indicated—or, if the interactions cannot be safely managed, an ID-selected rifampin-sparing regimen.
Recommends baseline liver tests and ongoing hepatotoxicity surveillance (symptom counseling and laboratory follow-up) when combining valproate with isoniazid, rifampin, and pyrazinamide.
